definitions.explanation: Describes a person, event, or circumstance that is favored by good fortune.

examples.japanese: {幸運|こううん}にも{怪我|けが}はなかった。
あの{事故|じこ}で{助|たす}かったのは{本当|ほんとう}に{幸運|こううん}なことだった。
examples.english: Surviving that accident was truly fortunate.

notes:
Composed of {幸|こう} (happiness, fortune) + {運|うん} (luck, fate). Can be used as a na-adjective ({幸運|こううん}な), as a noun ({幸運|こううん}), or adverbially ({幸運|こううん}にも). The adverbial form {幸運|こううん}にも (fortunately) is extremely common in both spoken and written Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幸運|こううん}にも: fortunately, luckily
- {幸運|こううん}を{祈|いの}る: to wish someone good luck
- {幸運|こううん}に{恵|めぐ}まれる: to be blessed with good fortune
- {幸運|こううん}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}: a lucky person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ラッキー: lucky — casual loanword used in everyday conversation
- {幸|さいわ}い: fortunately, luckily — adverbial use similar to {幸運|こううん}にも but slightly more formal
- {運|うん}がいい: lucky — a more colloquial way to say someone is lucky
- {不運|ふうん}な: unlucky, unfortunate — the antonym
